question:
Are there more in-patient or outpatient who were male? What is the deviation in percentage?
Benchmark knowledge evidence: male refers to SEX = 'M'; in-patient refers to Admission = '+'; outpatient refers to Admission = '-'; percentage = DIVIDE(COUNT(ID) where SEX = 'M' and Admission = '+', COUNT(ID) where SEX  = 'M' and Admission = '-')

auxiliary_raw_evidence_draft.base_sql:
WITH male_counts AS (
    SELECT
        SUM(CASE WHEN e.XCL_006 = 'Inpatient' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inpatient_male,
        SUM(CASE WHEN e.XCL_006 = 'Outpatient' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS outpatient_male
    FROM Examination e
    JOIN Patient p ON e.XCL_001 = p.XCL_058
    WHERE p.XCL_063 = 'M'
),
total_counts AS (
    SELECT
        SUM(CASE WHEN e.XCL_006 = 'Inpatient' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inpatient_total,
        SUM(CASE WHEN e.XCL_006 = 'Outpatient' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS outpatient_total
    FROM Examination e
)
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN mc.inpatient_male * 1.0 / tc.inpatient_total > mc.outpatient_male * 1.0 / tc.outpatient_total THEN 'Inpatient'
        ELSE 'Outpatient'
    END AS more_male_type,
    ABS(mc.inpatient_male * 1.0 / tc.inpatient_total - mc.outpatient_male * 1.0 / tc.outpatient_total) * 100 AS deviation_percentage
FROM male_counts mc
CROSS JOIN total_counts tc

  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN XCL_059 = 'M' AND XCL_063 = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) >
         SUM(CASE WHEN XCL_059 = 'M' AND XCL_063 = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    THEN 'in-patient'
    ELSE 'outpatient'
  END AS more_type,
  (SUM(CASE WHEN XCL_059 = 'M' AND XCL_063 = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) -
   SUM(CASE WHEN XCL_059 = 'M' AND XCL_063 = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) * 100.0 /
  SUM(CASE WHEN XCL_059 = 'M' AND XCL_063 = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS deviation_percentage
FROM Patient;
